title: Rolling Average on Daily Sales
prompt: Given s = pd.Series([10, 20, 30, 40], index=pd.date_range('2026-01-01', periods=4, freq='D')), compute rolling_2 = s.rolling(2).mean().tolist()[1:] (the valid 2-day rolling averages).
solution:
import pandas as pd
s = pd.Series([10, 20, 30, 40], index=pd.date_range('2026-01-01', periods=4, freq='D'))
rolling_2 = s.rolling(2).mean().tolist()[1:]
explanation: The first rolling(2) entry is NaN because 2 observations are needed; slicing [1:] gives [15.0, 25.0, 35.0].

title: resample() vs rolling()
solution: resample() groups into calendar frequency buckets; rolling() computes a sliding window over consecutive points.
back: `.resample()` aggregates into time-frequency buckets (e.g., daily to monthly); `.rolling()` computes a sliding window across consecutive rows.
